clue.text: Drink after expert has a breakdown

indicators.note: the drink is placed after the expert in the answer

parts.note: a crack shot or crack player is an expert
to sup is to drink, in sips

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink after an expert suffers a collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is an idiom for collapsing mentally, suffering a nervous breakdown.

clue.text: Measure length between Parisian street and river

indicators.note: the length sits between letters of the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Someone measures a length between a Paris street and the Seine.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a graduated strip for measuring length, a measuring instrument.

clue.text: Talk to an eccentric, bringing up a grand old city in Tennessee

parts.note: to chat is to talk

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the two little words are rearranged
in a down entry, bringing letters up reads them from bottom to top

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A chat with an oddball, raising the subject of a grand old Tennessee city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' turns TO AN into TANO; 'bringing up' turns A, G, O into OGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattanooga is a city in southeastern Tennessee, famous from the Chattanooga Choo Choo song.

clue.text: Foil may be kept in this British pub stuffing fish?

definitions.text: Foil may be kept in this

indicators.note: the British pub fills the fish, going inside it

parts.note: the scad is a fish, the horse mackerel
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Kitchen foil holds a British pub dish of stuffed fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' suggests kitchen wrap, but it is a fencing sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath for a blade, and a foil is a fencing sword that could rest in one.

clue.text: Dessert: exceptionally good thing Danes cooked best?

parts.note: a peach is something excellent, as in a peach of a shot

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters of Danes are reworked

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: A pudding asking whether Danes cook the finest treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaches and cream is a classic dessert of sliced fruit with cream.

clue.text: Type of betting odds to study

parts.note: SP stands for starting price, the betting odds at a race's start
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A punter learns about a kind of wagering odds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Type of betting', not 'Type of betting odds': spread betting stakes money on a range of outcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread betting is a form of gambling on whether a result falls above or below a quoted range.

clue.text: Lying down: touch of unease in back

indicators.note: the small bit goes inside the back

parts.note: the spine is the backbone, the back

indicators.note: a touch is a small bit, here the first letter of unease

explanation.surface: Someone lying down feels a twinge of unease in the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on the back, face upward, so a kind of lying down.

clue.text: Deserter, sailor, capsized

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down entry the word is turned over

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, short for tarpaulin

explanation.surface: A deserting sailor's boat overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who deserts a cause, as rats are said to leave a sinking ship.

clue.text: Steward, at end of event, remarkably tanned

indicators.note: the end of the word event is its last letter
remarkably suggests something surprising, so the letters of tanned are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steward at an event's close looks strikingly suntanned.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward serves passengers or guests, and an attendant is someone employed to wait on them.

clue.text: Animal from mountain area, tailless cat

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: without a tail, so the final letter of the word cat is lost

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A creature comes down from the mountains, a cat without a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American camelid kept for its wool, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Favourite Italian devoured by primate with relish

indicators.note: the primate swallows the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A favourite Italian dish is eaten greedily by an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish as a noun means keen enjoyment or zest, much as an appetite for something is eagerness for it.

clue.text: Strength of character shown in Educating Rita

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the play title's two words

explanation.surface: A quality displayed in Willy Russell's play Educating Rita.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, a synonym for strength of character.

clue.text: Responsible for factory worker being late

parts.note: to be behind a scheme is to be responsible for it
a hand is a manual worker, as in factory hand

explanation.surface: The person accountable for a factory employee running late.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand is an adjective meaning in arrears or behind schedule, so a synonym for late.

clue.text: Knave won — he's excited, truly

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: The rogue has won and he's thrilled, honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an idiomatic emphatic phrase used to mean certainly or indeed, much like truly.

clue.text: Outraged at university, current members

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
in means fashionable or current
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Present students and members of a university are outraged.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in arms is an idiom for protesting angrily, so being outraged.

clue.text: Something old to write on exercises clever people inside

indicators.note: the clever people go inside the exercises

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercises
arch means knowing or cunning
men are people

explanation.surface: An old writing surface gets clever people to do exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin, used as a writing material before paper became common.

clue.text: A street apart

parts.note: a way is a road or street, as in Broadway

explanation.surface: A road set apart from others.
explanation.definitionFit: Away and apart both mean at a distance or separated from something.

clue.text: High-speed train in news report

parts.note: the bullet train is Japan's high-speed railway

explanation.surface: A fast train features in a news broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news statement or broadcast.

clue.text: Group of singers heading for teeming Brazilian city

indicators.note: the head of the word teeming is its first letter

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, usually shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: A band of vocalists travels to the crowded Brazilian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, here three performers singing together.

clue.text: Name a custom, at Eton originally, in disgust

parts.note: use is custom or habit, as in usage

indicators.note: the original letter of Eton is its first

explanation.surface: Someone names a tradition of Eton, the English public school, and is appalled.
explanation.definitionFit: To nauseate is to sicken or revolt, a verb synonym of disgust.

clue.text: Source of pleasure? Fawlty finally in agreement!

parts.note: a treat is something that gives pleasure

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Fawlty

explanation.surface: A pleasure seeker sees Basil Fawlty, of the sitcom Fawlty Towers, at last agree.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: Melodramatic article on a hearing involving clubs

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the hearing takes in the clubs, holding them inside

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a court case involving nightclubs is overdramatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical behaviour is exaggerated and showy, as on a stage, which is melodramatic.

clue.text: Strip first of engines in aircraft

parts.note: a football team's strip is its kit

indicators.note: the first letter of the word engines is taken

explanation.surface: A mechanic strips the first of the engines from a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is RAF slang for an aeroplane, as well as the toy that flies on a string.

clue.text: Row about good dynamic person

indicators.note: the row goes about, around, the good

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A quarrel about a good, energetic person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is used figuratively for a fierce, energetic go-getter.

clue.text: Set off from aforementioned college in time

indicators.note: the college is placed inside the time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton, the college already named in the clue to 19 across

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the college just mentioned on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like departing, but it means to explode.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to make it explode, which is to detonate it.

clue.text: Have feathers daughter plucked

indicators.note: plucked means pulled out, as feathers are, so the daughter is removed

parts.note: down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: A daughter has her feathers plucked.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have or possess it.

clue.text: Difficult locking in right channel

indicators.note: the difficult word shuts the right inside itself

parts.note: tough means difficult, as in a tough job

explanation.surface: A hard job, securing the right channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long narrow channel or gutter for carrying water.

clue.text: Mean swindle by unknown character

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick or swindle
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted fraud is pulled off by a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of miserly or ungenerous with money is a synonym of stingy.

clue.text: Short skirts test the clergy!

parts.note: minis are miniskirts
to try is to test

explanation.surface: Miniskirts put the clergy's tolerance to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: The ministry is the body of ministers of religion, which is the clergy collectively.
